fields.value: Share evaluation machines and inference servers across experiments

EXP-66 groups an experiment's queued eval jobs onto one machine with one inference server. Sharing stops at the experiment: two experiments evaluating at the same time each rent and each load their own models.

Outcome: eval work from different experiments can share a machine and its inference server, and there is a way to define what exists outside any one experiment file.

Jack Heart, 2026-11-14: "I am okay with it currently being limited to sharing within one experiment but that is not ideal. Even if we do that there will definitely need to be a follow-up task, which is looking at having shared evaluation machines across experiments." And: "I'm not sure that we have the tools to do that with our current API since there isn't really any way to define anything as it exists outside the experiment file. That said we could also add that. We could add an additional API for this. It's worth having. We're going to need it".

Open (nothing accepted): what the outside-the-experiment API declares (a standing eval machine or pool, a served model, a shared budget) and where it is written, given that an experiment is one Python file with fixed declarations; who pays when experiments share a machine, since EXP-66 puts the dollar limit on the experiment; whether the scheduler or a controller above experiments decides the sharing; how results stay attributed (EXP-66 keeps them keyed by experiment, tournament and match). Related: EXP-66's note that launcher records live on one computer, so two computers do not see each other's queued work.
